rv.q: This is laughter-making on an industrial scale (to adapt a phrase) and it's a farce with fangs.
He has penned a vitriolic, bluntly entertaining comedy that initially has the audience tickled pink with its levity, then finally blushing red with national shame.

Richard Bean doesn't do things by halves. His new satirical comedy has a go at press, police and politicians, and covers just about every scandal of the past five years from phone-hacking to MPs' expenses.
About one out of every 50 is pretty funny.

cn.t: Richard Bean's timely satirical comedy delivers a bracing, verve-filled takedown of the phone-hacking scandal and the cosy corruption between press, police, and politicians that resonates with topical energy.
